items.program_name: Solar Billing Plan (Schedule NBT)
items.incentive_structure: Hourly Energy Export Credit at ACC values, plus Energy Export Bonus Credit (ACC Plus adder) for residential systems receiving PTO before 2028
items.event_limits: Residential Energy Export Bonus Credit locked at PTO and paid for 9 years; available only to customers on the Solar Billing Plan before 2028. Business customers moved to SBP billing March 2026
items.on_peak_window: Required import rate: E-ELEC (Electric Home), peak 4-9 p.m. daily
items.export_compensation: Hourly Energy Export Credit set from CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator; 8760 hourly values published per year (2023-2026 sheets posted); + ACC Plus adder for residential pre-2028 adopters
items.stackable_with: SGIP; ELRP/Power Saver Rewards; SmartRate

items.program_name: Solar Billing Plan (Net Billing Tariff)
items.incentive_structure: Hourly export credit at ACC values, plus ACC Plus adder for residential systems interconnecting before end of 2027
items.event_limits: ACC Plus adder paid for 9 years; not available to customers required to install solar by building code
items.export_compensation: Hourly export credit at CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator values; + ACC Plus adder for residential pre-2028 adopters; net surplus at wholesale
items.stackable_with: SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

items.program_name: Solar Billing Plan (Net Billing Tariff)
items.incentive_structure: Hourly export credit at ACC values
items.event_limits: No ACC Plus adder - CPUC excluded SDG&E residential customers because SDG&E's higher retail rates already produce larger bill savings
items.export_compensation: Hourly export credit at CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator values; NO ACC Plus adder; net surplus at wholesale
items.stackable_with: SGIP; ELRP/Power Saver Rewards

items.program_name: Schedule E-ELEC - Residential Time-of-Use (Electric Home)
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + daily income-tiered Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge (eff 2026-03-01): $0.19713/day Income Tier 1, $0.39688/day Tier 2, $0.79343/day Tier 3. CA Climate Credit $36.18/household semiannual
items.event_limits: Mandatory rate for residential Net Billing Tariff customers. Otherwise requires a qualifying technology: EV, energy storage (>=2 kWh, or >=0.05% of annual kWh if usage >6,000 kWh/yr), or electric heat pump
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule E-ELEC (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61545-E; Advice 7975-E eff 2026-08-28; rates per Advice 7921-E eff 2026-06-01)
items.on_peak_window: Peak 4-9pm every day incl weekends/holidays; Part-peak 3-4pm and 9pm-12am; Off-peak all other hours. Summer = Jun 1-Sep 30
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.55214 / part-peak $0.39026 / off-peak $0.33358 per kWh; winter peak $0.32063 / part-peak $0.29854 / off-peak $0.28468
items.export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT if on Solar Billing Plan; E-ELEC also open to legacy NEM/NEM2 customers with a qualifying technology
items.stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan (NBT); NEM/NEM2; SGIP; ELRP

items.program_name: Schedule E-TOU-C - Residential Time-of-Use (Peak Pricing 4-9 p.m. Every Day)
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with baseline credit + daily income-tiered Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Baseline credit $0.08140/kWh on baseline usage; Base Services Charge $0.19713 / $0.39688 / $0.79343 per day by income tier (eff 2026-03-01)
items.event_limits: Bill protection closed to customers enrolling after 2022-05-04
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule E-TOU-C (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61124-E, eff 2026-03-01; rates Advice 7921-E eff 2026-06-01)
items.on_peak_window: Peak 4-9pm all days year-round; Off-peak all other times. Summer = Jun 1-Sep 30
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.52240 / off-peak $0.39940; winter peak $0.39757 / off-peak $0.36757 per kWh; less $0.08140/kWh baseline credit
items.export_compensation: Not a solar tariff by itself - export terms come from NEM2 or Schedule NBT
items.stackable_with: NEM2; SmartRate; SmartAC

items.program_name: Schedule EV2 (EV2-A) - Residential Time-of-Use for Plug-in Electric Vehicle Customers
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with a very wide peak/off-peak spread + daily income-tiered Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge $0.19713 / $0.39688 / $0.79343 per day by income tier (eff 2026-03-01)
items.event_limits: Storage-only enrollment is a PILOT capped at 30,000 storage-only customers; battery must be >=2 kWh (or >=0.05% of annual kWh above 6,000 kWh/yr). Whole-premise usage above 800% of baseline over 12 months forces removal to E-TOU-D and a 12-month ban from EV rates
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule EV2 (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61169-E eff 2026-03-01; rates Advice 7921-E eff 2026-06-01)
items.on_peak_window: Peak 4-9pm every day; Part-peak 3-4pm and 9pm-12am; Off-peak all other hours. Summer = Jun 1-Sep 30
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.53809 / part-peak $0.42760 / off-peak $0.22558; winter peak $0.41099 / part-peak $0.39428 / off-peak $0.22558 per kWh
items.export_compensation: Not a solar tariff by itself; NEM2 customers may take EV2
items.stackable_with: NEM2; SGIP; ELRP

items.program_name: Schedule TOU-D Option 4-9PM (TOU-D-4-9PM)
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + baseline credit + daily Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Baseline credit $0.10/kWh up to monthly baseline allocation; Base Services Charge $0.79/day. Extra baseline allocation for heat-pump water heater customers (1.9 kWh/day summer, 2.6 kWh/day winter)
items.event_limits: Switching onto a TOU rate locks the customer out of another rate change for 12 months
items.on_peak_window: Summer (Jun-Sep): On-peak weekdays 4-9pm; weekend 4-9pm is Mid-peak; Off-peak all other. Winter (Oct-May): Super-off-peak 8am-4pm, Mid-peak 4-9pm, Off-peak all other
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Summer weekday on-peak 58c / off-peak 34c; summer weekend mid-peak 46c / off-peak 34c; winter mid-peak 51c / super-off-peak 33c / off-peak 37c per kWh (SCE-published rounded values, no effective date shown on page; subtract 10c baseline credit within allocation)
items.export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT or NEM2, depending on vintage
items.stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan; NEM2; SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

items.program_name: Schedule TOU-D Option 5-8PM (TOU-D-5-8PM)
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + baseline credit + daily Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Baseline credit $0.10/kWh up to monthly baseline allocation; Base Services Charge $0.79/day
items.event_limits: 12-month lock-in after a rate switch
items.on_peak_window: Summer (Jun-Sep): On-peak weekdays 5-8pm; weekend 5-8pm Mid-peak; Off-peak all other. Winter (Oct-May): Super-off-peak 8am-4pm, Mid-peak 5-8pm, Off-peak all other
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Summer weekday on-peak 74c / off-peak 34c; summer weekend mid-peak 54c / off-peak 34c; winter mid-peak 60c / super-off-peak 32c / off-peak 38c per kWh (SCE-published rounded values, no effective date shown on page)
items.stackable_with: NEM2; SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

items.program_name: Schedule TOU-D Option PRIME (TOU-D-PRIME)
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with wide peak/off-peak spread + daily Base Services Charge; no baseline credit
items.incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge $0.79/day; no baseline credit
items.event_limits: MANDATORY rate for SCE Solar Billing Plan (NBT) customers. Otherwise requires attestation of EV/PHEV ownership or lease, a residential battery, or an electric heat pump for water or space heating. 12-month lock-in after switching
items.on_peak_window: Summer (Jun-Sep): On-peak weekdays 4-9pm; weekend 4-9pm Mid-peak; Off-peak all other. Winter (Oct-May): Super-off-peak 8am-4pm, Mid-peak 4-9pm, Off-peak all other
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Summer weekday on-peak 59c / off-peak 26c; summer weekend mid-peak 40c / off-peak 26c; winter mid-peak 56c / super-off-peak 24c / off-peak 24c per kWh (SCE-published rounded values, no effective date shown on page)
items.export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT (hourly ACC export credit + ACC Plus adder)
items.stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan; SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

items.program_name: Schedule TOU-D Options A, B and T (discontinued TOU periods)
items.incentive_structure: Legacy TOU rate options
items.event_limits: Closed to new enrollment; existing customers may stay but cannot return once they leave
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule TOU-D Options A / B / T
items.on_peak_window: Legacy TOU periods (not the 4-9pm or 5-8pm structure)
items.stackable_with: NEM2

items.program_name: Schedule TOU-DR1 - Residential Time of Use Service
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + baseline adjustment credit + daily Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Baseline Adjustment Credit $0.10905/kWh up to 130% of baseline; Base Services Charge $0.79343/day standard, $0.39688/day for CARE(DRAH) and FERA (eff 2026-01-01)
items.event_limits: SDG&E states TOU-DR1 is its standard residential schedule
items.on_peak_window: On-Peak 4-9pm; Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak all other hours. Summer = Jun-Oct
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Total eff 2026-01-01: summer on-peak $0.69654 / off-peak $0.47560 / super-off-peak $0.38818; winter on-peak $0.62200 / off-peak $0.54019 / super-off-peak $0.44933 per kWh
items.export_compensation: Per NEM2 or Schedule NBT depending on vintage
items.stackable_with: NEM2; SGIP; ELRP

items.program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (PG&E, administered via Olivine)
items.incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment
items.incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh of measured load reduction (non-residential, per CPUC ELRP terms)
items.event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap
items.stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program (Group B, incremental only)

items.program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (SCE)
items.incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment
items.incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh of measured load reduction (non-residential, per CPUC ELRP terms)
items.event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap
items.stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program (Group B, incremental only); Smart Energy Program

items.program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (SDG&E)
items.incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment
items.incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh of measured load reduction (non-residential, per CPUC ELRP terms)
items.event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap
items.stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program (Group B, incremental only)

items.program_name: Schedule E-BIP - Base Interruptible Program
items.incentive_structure: $/kW-month capacity payment on Potential Load Reduction, with $/kWh penalty for energy above Firm Service Level
items.incentive_value_usd: 15-Minute BIP: Nov-Apr $10.60 (1-500 kW) / $11.20 (501-1,000 kW) / $11.80 (>1,000 kW) per kW-month; May-Oct $13.60 / $14.20 / $14.80 per kW-month. 30-Minute BIP: Nov-Apr $9.50 / $10.00 / $10.50; May-Oct $12.50 / $13.00 / $13.50 per kW-month. Rates effective 2025-05-17 (Advice 7572-E); D.23-12-005 authorized the $2/kW May-Oct adder for 2024-2027. Excess Energy Charge $6.00/kWh above Firm Service Level ($8.40/kWh after a failed re-test)
items.event_limits: Max 1 event/day, 6 hours max per event, max 10 events/calendar month, 180 hours/calendar year; year-round; 15- or 30-minute notice. Two utility test events per year count as program events. Requires >=100 kW max demand and FSL <=85% of highest monthly max demand, minimum 100 kW reduction
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule E-BIP (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61454-E et seq.; Advice 7942-E eff 2026-07-10, Res. E-5451)
items.on_peak_window: Dispatch triggered by CAISO market award / Operating Procedure 4420, or PG&E T&D reliability need; measured against summer on-peak / winter on-peak or partial-peak demand
items.peak_offpeak_rates: n/a - capacity payment, not a rate
items.export_compensation: Customers on Net Energy Metering schedules (except NEMCCSF) are eligible
items.stackable_with: STACKS WITH: ELRP, Schedule E-SLRP, and (legacy dual enrollments only) Peak Day Pricing. PROHIBITED with any other capacity-based program including the Capacity Bidding Program

items.program_name: Underfrequency Relay (UFR) Program (rider to Schedule E-BIP)
items.incentive_structure: $/kW-month demand credit for automatic underfrequency interruption
items.incentive_value_usd: $0.67/kW-month demand credit on average monthly summer on-peak / winter partial-peak demand
items.event_limits: Automatic interruption when system frequency drops to 59.65 Hz for 20 cycles. Direct-enrolled customers only (not available through DR aggregators). PG&E may require up to 3 years written notice to terminate
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule E-BIP, Underfrequency Relay Program section
items.stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program

items.program_name: Schedule E-CBP - Capacity Bidding Program
items.incentive_structure: Monthly $/kW capacity payment on nominated load plus $/kWh energy payment for delivered event curtailment; paid to the aggregator, who sets customer compensation
items.event_limits: Aggregator-managed and integrated into CAISO as a Proxy Demand Resource (PDR). Season May 1 - Oct 31. 'Elect' option: max 1 event/day, 4-hour max event duration, participant may elect more than 6 events/month. Day-ahead notification by 5 p.m. Triggered by a CAISO market award for the CBP PDR. NO minimum demand requirement. Net-metered, partial-standby, Auto-DR, bundled, DA and CCA customers eligible; full-standby, WAPA-served and NEMCCSF customers are not
items.tariff_schedule: Schedule E-CBP (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 49623-E; Advice 6160-E, D.21-03-056)
items.on_peak_window: May 1 - Oct 31 event windows, day-ahead notice
items.stackable_with: May dual-participate with Schedule E-OBMC and with ELRP Group B (incremental reduction only). NOT compatible with the Base Interruptible Program (both are capacity-based)

items.program_name: Peak Day Pricing (PDP)
items.incentive_structure: Summer rate discount in exchange for a high event-day surcharge
items.event_limits: 9 to 15 Peak Day Pricing Event Days per year, typically the hottest summer days. New dual enrollment with the Base Interruptible Program has not been available since 2018-10-26
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Summer rates are discounted; effective rates are higher during PDP event hours (specific credit and surcharge values published in the underlying rate schedules, not on the program page)
items.stackable_with: Automated Demand Response; legacy BIP dual enrollment only

items.program_name: Schedule E-OBMC - Optional Binding Mandatory Curtailment Plan
items.incentive_structure: No cash incentive - the benefit is exemption from rotating outages; penalty-only structure
items.incentive_value_usd: $0 incentive; $6.00/kWh penalty for each kWh above the commitment
items.event_limits: Must reduce entire circuit load 5-15% within 15 minutes of alert (eligibility requires ability to achieve 15% below baseline). Events any day including weekends/holidays with no frequency or duration limit. Second failure in a 1-year period terminates the plan and bars re-entry for 5 years
items.on_peak_window: Any day, any hour, no cap
items.stackable_with: Capacity Bidding Program

items.program_name: Automated Demand Response (ADR) incentive
items.incentive_structure: Upfront $/kW incentive for OpenADR-capable automation, capped as a share of project cost
items.incentive_value_usd: $200/kW for approved projects, up to 75% of eligible project costs
items.event_limits: Requires enrollment in an eligible PG&E DR program (Peak Day Pricing or Capacity Bidding Program), OpenADR 2.0a/2.0b capability, 12 months billing history, and a 3-year (Standard option 1) or 5-year (option 2) participation commitment
items.stackable_with: REQUIRES co-enrollment in Peak Day Pricing or the Capacity Bidding Program

items.program_name: Automated Response Technology (ART)
items.incentive_structure: Incentive set and paid by the third-party ART provider, not by PG&E
items.event_limits: Events may occur at any time and last 1 to 4 hours in a single day; day-ahead email notification. Enrollment is via a third-party provider. Batteries may export stored energy to the grid during events
items.export_compensation: Battery may send energy to the grid during program events
items.stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with SmartRate, SmartAC, WatterSaver and other PG&E residential DR - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

items.program_name: SmartRate (residential critical peak pricing)
items.incentive_structure: Summer rate discount plus a high per-kWh surcharge during SmartRate event hours, with a first-year Bill Protection guarantee
items.event_limits: PG&E's page states SmartRate is 'risk free and backed by our Bill Protection guarantee'; the per-kWh credit and event surcharge are set in the underlying rate schedule and were not retrievable from the published tariff PDF path tested
items.stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with other PG&E residential DR programs - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

items.program_name: SmartAC
items.incentive_structure: Bill credit for utility-controlled A/C cycling via a SmartAC switch
items.event_limits: Requires a central air conditioning unit; PG&E remotely shifts A/C load out of peak hours
items.stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with other PG&E residential DR programs - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

items.program_name: WatterSaver
items.incentive_structure: Enrollment bonus plus monthly participation credit
items.incentive_value_usd: $50 gift card enrollment bonus plus $5 gift card credit for every month of participation
items.event_limits: Requires an electric water heater; heating is shifted automatically to lower-cost hours
items.on_peak_window: Shifts water heating out of high-price hours
items.stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with other PG&E residential DR programs - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

items.program_name: Behind-the-Meter Optimization of Load Technology (BOLT) Study
items.incentive_structure: One-time enrollment bonus plus a post-participation reward, per device
items.incentive_value_usd: Behind-the-meter batteries up to $400 each; electric vehicles up to $125 each; smart thermostats up to $100 each. No device limit. Rewards paid in two stages (enrollment bonus, then after study participation)
items.event_limits: Study, not a permanent tariff. Enrollment through study partners EnergyHub, Octopus or Uplight/Optiwatt. EV participants must have home charging
items.tariff_schedule: Behind-the-Meter Optimization of Load Technology Study
items.stackable_with: Runs through third-party aggregators; interaction with Smart Energy Program / Summer Discount Plan not stated on SCE's page

items.program_name: Smart Energy Program (SEP)
items.incentive_structure: One-time sign-up bill credit plus annual bill credits for thermostat events
items.incentive_value_usd: $75 one-time sign-up credit plus up to $50/year in bill credits for maintaining enrollment June 1 - Sept 30
items.event_limits: Requires a qualifying smart thermostat with a central A/C system. SCE raises the thermostat setpoint up to 4 degrees during events; customer may override any event at any time
items.stackable_with: SCE states customers may be enrolled in only one A/C-based program at a time (SEP or Summer Discount Plan)

items.program_name: Summer Discount Plan (SDP)
items.incentive_structure: Monthly summer bill credits for utility-controlled A/C cycling
items.incentive_value_usd: Up to $160/year in summer bill credits
items.event_limits: Requires a central A/C system. SCE cycles the A/C off and on during events. The 'override' program option allows opting out of up to 5 events per year. Credits earned June 1 - Sept 30
items.stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with the Smart Energy Program

items.program_name: Capacity Bidding Program - Elect (CBP-E) and CBP-E Direct
items.incentive_structure: Capacity Payments plus Energy Payments; for CBP-E the aggregator sets what the customer receives
items.incentive_value_usd: Aggregator-determined for CBP-E; CBP-E Direct pays based on event performance
items.event_limits: Summer-only, event-based. CBP-E Direct credits earned May 1 - Oct 31. Open to all customer classes
items.stackable_with: Aggregator-mediated; SCE lists AutoGrid, EnergyHub, Enersponse, Leap and Stem as third-party DR providers in its territory

items.program_name: Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) - residential and non-residential
items.incentive_structure: Monthly summer bill credits in exchange for much higher energy rates during CPP events
items.incentive_value_usd: SCE states average savings around $50/year for residential participants
items.event_limits: 12-15 CPP events per year, 4 p.m. to 9 p.m.; events may be called year-round including weekends and holidays. Monthly bill credits earned June 1 - Sept 30. First-year bill protection: total paid will not exceed what the customer would have paid on their prior rate. No penalties for not curtailing
items.tariff_schedule: Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate option; requires a TOU rate and Bundled Service from SCE
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Event-hour energy rates are significantly higher than the underlying TOU rate
items.stackable_with: Requires SCE bundled service on a TOU rate; not available to CCA or Direct Access generation customers

items.program_name: SmartShift Rewards
items.incentive_structure: Enrollment reward plus monthly participation payments
items.incentive_value_usd: $100 enrollment reward plus $5 to $10 per month of participation (SCE's comparison table cites a $50 sign-up credit and about $60/year average)
items.event_limits: Year-round. Heat pump water heaters require a thermostatic mixing valve and WiFi; electric resistance water heaters require WiFi (a free external communication device is available). Must be connected at least 2 weeks each month to earn the reward. Opt out at any time
items.stackable_with: Unknown

items.program_name: Charge Smart - SoCal (managed EV charging, operated with WeaveGrid)
items.incentive_structure: Sign-up bonus plus annual reward for allowing managed off-peak charging
items.incentive_value_usd: $50 sign-up bonus plus $50 annually for up to three years
items.event_limits: Compatible with most smart chargers and Teslas. Customers may override the charging schedule at any time via dashboard or by texting 'Charge Now'. No penalty for opting out. SCE's cited ~$650/yr combined figure assumes TOU-D-PRIME off-peak charging, 12,000 miles/yr and 3.7 mi/kWh
items.stackable_with: Designed around TOU-D-PRIME

items.program_name: Schedule EV-TOU-5 - Domestic Time-of-Use for Households with Electric Vehicles
items.incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with a very deep super-off-peak period, plus a daily Base Services Charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge $0.79343/day standard, $0.39688/day CARE(DRAH) and FERA
items.event_limits: MANDATORY import rate for SDG&E Solar Billing Plan (NBT) customers. Otherwise requires a qualifying EV registered with the California DMV (or a natural gas home fueling pump)
items.on_peak_window: On-Peak 4-9pm; Super Off-Peak overnight/midday; Off-Peak all other. Summer = Jun-Oct
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Total eff 2026-08-01: summer on-peak $0.80205 / off-peak $0.49627 / super-off-peak $0.13090; winter on-peak $0.52383 / off-peak $0.46566 / super-off-peak $0.12332 per kWh
items.export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT (hourly ACC export credit, no ACC Plus adder) or NEM2 depending on vintage
items.stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan; SGIP; ELRP A.4

items.program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program A.4 - residential battery storage
items.incentive_structure: Per-event compensation for battery discharge, PAID BY THE BATTERY MANUFACTURER rather than by SDG&E
items.event_limits: Events may be called any day of the week, 4-9 p.m., May through October; events last 1 to 3 hours. Triggered when CAISO issues an Emergency Energy Alert; SDG&E notifies the battery manufacturer, which dispatches the fleet. Enrollment is ONLY through a participating battery storage manufacturer. Available to bundled, Direct Access and CCA customers. Authority: CPUC D.21-12-015
items.peak_offpeak_rates: n/a - event compensation set by the battery manufacturer
items.export_compensation: Battery discharges to serve load and/or export during events
items.stackable_with: STACKS WITH the Time-of-Use Plus (TOU-DR-P) pricing plan. NOT compatible with a Rule 32 program. Enrolling in ELRP A.4 un-enrolls the customer from Power Saver Rewards

items.program_name: Power Saver Rewards (SDG&E residential ELRP A.6)
items.incentive_structure: $/kWh bill credit for load reduction during 4-9 p.m. events
items.incentive_value_usd: $1.00/kWh of measured incremental load reduction while the program operated (CPUC ELRP A.6 rate)
items.event_limits: SDG&E stopped accepting applications as of 2025-11-01 and unenrolled participating customers; the program does not continue in 2026. Matches the CPUC statement that residential ELRP sunsets at the end of the 2025 program year
items.stackable_with: Superseded for battery owners by ELRP A.4

items.program_name: Schedule B-19 - Medium General Demand-Metered TOU Service (standard rate)
items.incentive_structure: Monthly $/kW demand charges (time-related peak/part-peak plus non-coincident maximum demand) + TOU energy + daily customer charge
items.incentive_value_usd: Secondary voltage, eff 2026-03-01: Maximum Peak Demand Summer $46.16/kW; Maximum Part-Peak Demand Summer $10.52/kW; Maximum Demand Summer $37.37/kW; Maximum Peak Demand Winter $2.31/kW; Maximum Demand Winter $37.37/kW. Primary voltage $37.89 / $8.54 / $29.11 / $1.69 / $29.11 per kW. Customer charge $58.62824/meter/day mandatory B-19, $11.36882/day voluntary B-19
items.event_limits: Mandatory for customers whose maximum billing demand exceeded 499 kW for at least three consecutive months in the most recent 12 (and below the B-20 threshold). Demand is averaged over 15-minute intervals
items.on_peak_window: SUMMER (Jun 1-Sep 30): Peak 4-9pm every day incl weekends/holidays; Partial-Peak 2-4pm and 9-11pm every day; Off-Peak all other. WINTER (Oct 1-May 31): Peak 4-9pm every day; Super Off-Peak 9am-2pm every day in March, April and May; Off-Peak all other
items.peak_offpeak_rates: Secondary voltage energy eff 2026-03-01: summer peak $0.18648 / part-peak $0.14775 / off-peak $0.12037; winter peak $0.16188 / off-peak $0.12026 / super-off-peak $0.06442 per kWh

items.program_name: Schedule B-19 Option S (storage rate option)

items.program_name: Ancillary Services (Regulation Up/Down, Spinning Reserve, Non-Spinning Reserve) - reachability for BTM aggregations and DMM clearing prices
items.incentive_structure: $/MW-hour capacity payment at the Day-Ahead ancillary service market clearing price; Real-Time pays only incremental capacity above the DA award; rescinded (No-Pay) if the resource does not perform
items.incentive_value_usd: DMM quantity-weighted average clearing prices ($/MW per hour), 2024 -> 2025. Day-Ahead: Reg Up $4.37 -> $3.40; Reg Down $6.29 -> $7.51; Spin $4.18 -> $0.84; Non-Spin $1.96 -> $0.94. Real-Time: Reg Up $7.18 -> $10.14; Reg Down $7.15 -> $16.18; Spin $1.03 -> $0.80; Non-Spin $0.85 -> $0.85. About 90% of 2025 AS cost was incurred day-ahead. Total CAISO AS cost $94.5M in 2025 ($0.47/MWh of load). DMM: actual CAISO batteries earned about $9/kW-yr from regulation in 2025; batteries supplied 53% of AS requirements
items.event_limits: Which BTM participation models can reach which product (CAISO PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA comparison matrix): PDR - Spin and Non-Spin only (500 kW minimum curtailment sustainable 30 min; direct telemetry at any size); DERA/HDERA - Energy plus Spin and Non-Spin (modeled as generic NGR, NON-REM subtype per Order 2222 BRS BRQ-002; direct telemetry required at any size for AS); REGULATION UP/DOWN is listed only for the Non-Generator Resource (NGR) model (LESR/DDR subtypes; 500 kW minimum; 4-second telemetry with 8-second round trip; 60-min continuous energy non-REM or 15-min under REM), which requires the ISO interconnection and New Resource Implementation process and ISO- or SC-metering of the resource - i.e. not a retail-meter BTM aggregation path. RDRR and the PDR-LSR Consumption ID cannot provide any AS. All AS requires AS certification (Tariff Appendix K) and unannounced compliance testing (7% of resources failed in 2025)
items.tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Section 8 and Appendix K (Ancillary Service Requirements Protocol); Tariff 4.17.7; BPM for Market Instruments Section 3.2; BPM for Direct Telemetry; DMM 2025 Annual Report on Market Issues and Performance Chapter 12 (Figures 12.4 and 12.5)
items.stackable_with: Co-optimized with energy for the same resource. BTM battery aggregations realistically reach Spin/Non-Spin (via PDR or DERA) but not Regulation; Regulation needs a wholesale-metered NGR. RA-shown PDR can also sell Spin/Non-Spin

items.program_name: Heterogeneous DER Aggregation (HDERA) with Distributed Curtailment Resources - FERC Order 2222 model
items.incentive_structure: $/MWh LMP on the SUM of net DER energy injection plus DCR demand curtailment (curtailment metered as positive supply); settled as one generic NGR non-REM resource
items.event_limits: Live since November 1 2024 (Tariff 4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6). Must contain at least one Distributed Curtailment Resource (demand response) and may also contain injecting DERs. Minimum 100 kW aggregate Pmax. All locations in the same Sub-LAP; PNodes Pre-Defined (default GDFs) or Customized (DERP-specified GDFs summing to 1); GDFs may be resubmitted with hourly bids. Bids are subject to the same Net Benefits Test price threshold as PDR. DCR curtailment is measured against an ISO-approved baseline from Tariff 4.13.4 (weather matching, control group, day-matching 10-in-10 / 5-in-10 residential / combined, Meter Generator Output variants, EVSE residential/non-residential variants, PDR-LSR variants). SCME must submit net DER energy, DCR curtailment, the baseline used, and underlying hourly consumption for all baseline days. Any change to locations, capacity, baseline or SC requires a new UDC concurrence (Attachment A) submission
items.tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Sections 4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6, 4.13.4; FERC Order 2222 Business Requirements Specification v1.2 (Jun 28 2024) BRQ-002, BRQ-005, BRQ-008, BRQ-009, BRQ-106; BPM for Demand Response Section 5 (baselines)
items.export_compensation: Net DER injection + DCR curtailment both settled at PNode LMP
items.stackable_with: Energy + Spin/Non-Spin as for DERA. Same double-counting guard as DERA: DER on a retail NEM program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation is barred; UDC may raise double-counting concerns in its review

items.program_name: WEIM / EDAM - access for customer-sited batteries in non-CAISO California balancing areas (LADWP, BANC/SMUD, TID, IID)
items.incentive_structure: No direct CAISO payment to the customer or a third-party aggregator. In WEIM, demand response enters only as a Load Forecast Adjustment submitted by the WEIM Entity (the utility/BA) - implicitly valued as a self-schedule; the BA, not the DR provider, sees any real-time imbalance settlement
items.event_limits: Answer: effectively NO direct path. The CAISO retail-DR and DER aggregation models (PDR, PDR-LSR, RDRR, DERA/HDERA) are CAISO-balancing-area participation models. In a WEIM BAA the only CAISO-recognized DR mechanism is the WEIM Entity's Load Forecast Adjustment (no minimum size; aggregated across forecast zones within the WEIM BAA; 5-minute schedule submitted a day ahead and updated to T-45; WEIM Entity must sign a DR attestation per EIM BPM Appendix C; no telemetry requirement). A BTM battery can only reach WEIM value indirectly through the host utility's own DR/VPP program. Status of the host BAs: TID has been a WEIM participant since 2021; LADWP and BANC (incl. SMUD) are WEIM participants and signed EDAM implementation agreements (BANC Nov 22 2024; LADWP Jan 13 2025) for planned EDAM entry in 2027; TID signed May 19 2025 for 2027; IID signed May 22 2025 for 2028. EDAM went live May 1 2026 with PacifiCorp (PGE planned 2026). CAISO matrix notes a day-ahead LFA option pending EDAM tariff approval
items.tariff_schedule: CAISO Tariff Section 29 (WEIM), 29.34 (WEIM Entity load forecast / DR); EDAM Tariff Section 33; BPM for Energy Imbalance Market Appendix C (Demand Response Attestation); EDAM Implementation Agreements for BANC, LADWP, TID, IID
items.stackable_with: Only via the POU's own retail program (e.g. SMUD, LADWP, TID DR/VPP programs), which is outside CAISO. FERC Order 2222 DER aggregation rights attach to RTO/ISO balancing areas and do not reach these public-power BAs

items.program_name: Small utility opt-in gate and state aggregation rules for DER Aggregations
items.incentive_structure: Eligibility gate - no payment
items.event_limits: California has NOT opted out of third-party aggregation of retail customers; CPUC has permitted third-party Demand Response Providers to bid retail customers into CAISO as PDR since the DR direct-participation rules (Electric Rule 24 at PG&E/SCE, Rule 32 at SDG&E). The only Order 2222 gate is the small-utility provision: CAISO may not accept a DERA containing customers of a utility that distributed 4 million MWh or less in the prior fiscal year unless that utility's RERRA permits it (DERP Agreement Appendix B.21 Section 4.1.4; the same opt-in already existed in the pro forma Demand Response Provider Agreement). In practice this reaches small California publicly owned utilities and MSS operators inside the CAISO BAA. Separately a DER on a retail net energy metering program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation is barred from a DERA
